At 5’6” and a strict $3,500 CAD budget (including taxes), the Kona Ecoco is the clear winner—especially when purchased on sale, which leaves plenty of room for BC’s 12% combined PST/GST and a bolt-on rear rack.

Side-by-Side Comparison (Tailored for 5’6” & $3,500 CAD Tax-In)

Feature Kona Ecoco (Best Fit & Value) Norco Scene VLT (Over Budget at MSRP) Tern Vektron Q9 (Over Budget)
Brand Heritage Kona (Founded 1988 — 38 yrs) Norco (Founded 1964 — 62 yrs) Tern (Founded 2011; Dahon lineage 1982)
Recommended Size (5’6”) Small or Medium (Sits right on the cusp; S for upright/easy reach, M for longer leg extension) Small (Fits ~5’2”–5’7”) One Size Fits All (Fits riders 4’10”–6’5”)
Weight 43.0 lbs (19.5 kg) ~36–48 lbs (depending on build) 48.3 lbs (21.9 kg)
Removable Battery Yes — 504 Wh Shimano (ABUS lock) Yes — 504 Wh Shimano (keyed lock) Yes — 400 Wh Bosch PowerPack
Motor Shimano Mid-Drive (EP500 / E6100) Shimano STEPS EP6 Mid-Drive (85 Nm) Bosch Active Line Plus Mid-Drive (50 Nm)
Fenders Included (Full-wrap) Not included (Mounts ready) Included (SKS fenders)
Lights Included (Front & rear integrated) Included (Front & rear integrated) Included (Front & rear integrated)
Rear Rack Not included (Frame eyelets ready; ~$60–$90 aftermarket) Not included (Frame eyelets ready; ~$60–$90 aftermarket) Included (Atlas V Rack, 60 lb capacity)
Canadian Price (Before Tax) $2,475 – $2,640 CAD (Sale) / $3,299 CAD (MSRP) $3,699 CAD (MSRP) / ~$3,400 CAD (Sale) $4,199 – $4,649 CAD
Est. Total w/ 12% BC Tax ~$2,772 – $2,957 CAD (Sale) / ~$3,695 CAD (MSRP) ~$4,143 CAD (MSRP) / ~$3,808 CAD (Sale) ~$4,703 – $5,207 CAD
Fits $3,500 Tax-In Budget? Yes (When bought on current Canadian closeout/sale pricing) No (Exceeds $3,500 once 12% tax is added) No (Well over $3,500 before tax)

Key Takeaways for Your Setup

  • Best Overall Choice: Look for a Kona Ecoco (Size Small or Medium) on sale through Canadian dealers (such as PRFO Sports or Skiis & Biikes, currently listing around $2,475–$2,640 CAD). Even after adding 12% BC tax (~$300), a lightweight aluminum rear rack (~$75), and shipping/PDI (~$150), your total lands around $3,000–$3,200 CAD—comfortably under $3,500 while keeping total bike weight around 44.5 lbs.
  • Sizing Tip at 5’6”: Because 5’6” sits right on the overlap between Kona’s Small (5’2”–5’7”) and Medium (5’6”–5’10”), Size Small is generally preferred on a step-through commuter for a shorter reach to the swept-back handlebars and easier flat-footed stops.
